title: Latency thermocline probe - scratch notes
content:
Quick note: trying to capture a sketchy observation from last week's flakiness sweep.

Goal
- Understand layered (depth-wise) latency behavior across context length / KV cache hit fraction. This is my "thermocline" metaphor: a sharp boundary in distribution where latency characteristics change (like temperature layering in an ocean).

Hypothesis
- For requests with mixed context-lengths hitting the same worker, p50 behaves smoothly but p95/p99 jumps once active KV working set exceeds L2-like boundary (memory pressure + kernel path change).
- Small-LLM (7B-ish) with q8 exec path seems to flip to slower path after ~384 tokens of dense KV usage; large models show shift earlier due to kernel memory layout.

Testbed / env
- cluster: dedicated-dev-03 (a2-highmem prototype, 4x A100-sxm, NCCL/Driver: 525.125)
- runtime: serving-runtime/fleet-v2.9.1 (local builds with debug logging on)
- model: open-7b-q8 (redwood/open-7b-q8-v1) pinned commit: 2025-09-19
- client: loadgen v0.8.2 (http streaming disabled), run from jenkins-agent-5
- traffic shape: mix of short (16-32 tokens), medium (128-256), long (512-768) in 60/30/10 ratio; synthetic payloads, simple prompts.
- KV cache priming: warm priming enabled for a subset of runs (prefix=recent 512 tokens); tests include both cold-primed and hot-primed workers.

Commands (repro)
- start server: ./run_server --model open-7b-q8-v1 --max-seq 2048 --kv-cache true --quant q8
- run load: python bench/loadgen.py --qps 120 --duration 900 --pattern mixed-lengths.yaml --client-concurrency 32

Observations (raw)
- baseline (cold workers, unprimed): p50=42ms, p95=168ms, p99=360ms, throughput ~110 qps (client-limited at 120 target)
- primed workers (hot cache): p50=31ms, p95=110ms, p99=230ms, throughput steady ~118 qps
- mid-run flip: at t+12m saw a step increase in p99 to ~900ms for a 3m interval, then recovered. No pod restarts.
- CPU/GPU: during the spike GPU utilization stayed ~78-84% (no saturation). Notable host memory RSS spike (+20%) correlated with p99 bump.

Micro-analysis notes
- Kernel path toggling: /srv/logs/trace.log shows many entries of "kv_eviction_path invoked" around event. I suspect a fallback from the fast in-GPU page-resident KV handler to a slower host-IO-bound reconciler when working set crosses threshold.
- Device page faults? dmesg shows a handful of GPU page migration warnings (rare). Might be driver-level.
- Scheduling: cgroups show sudden increase in softirq latency during the episode. Possibly network interrupts interfering with batching window timings.

Simple table (representative snapshots)
- Snapshot A (hot, stable): [p50=31, p95=110, p99=230, qps=118]
- Snapshot B (cold-ish): [p50=42, p95=168, p99=360, qps=110]
- Snapshot C (event spike): [p50=38, p95=215, p99=900+, qps=95]

Quick experiment I ran (two short runs)
1) Lower batch timeout from 12ms -> 6ms: reduced p50 by ~4ms but p99 unchanged during spike window. Means spike not caused by batching holding requests.
2) Limit concurrent contexts per worker (soft cap 48 -> 28): p99 tail reduced during similar loads (peak p99 620ms vs 900ms), but throughput dropped to ~84 qps. Tradeoff ok for latency-critical flows.

Immediate conclusions
- There is a latent boundary (thermocline) where memory/KV working set growth triggers a slower codepath; this disproportionately hurts p99 while p50 remains acceptable.
- Short-term mitigation: keep per-worker active context cap, more aggressive pre-eviction heuristics for KV, and increase host GPU pinned memory to reduce page churn.
- Longer-term: need a kernel-level investigation (NVIDIA driver/UCX) and a runtime change to make the slow path less blocking (async reconciliation).

Open questions / TODOs
- Q: Is this specific to q8 quant path? Need same run with q4_hybrid to compare.
- Q: Are certain prompt shapes worse (dense repeated tokens)? Will sweep corpus diversity tomorrow.
- TODO: open a Linear ticket with the sample trace + dmesg + perf profile (link above).
- TODO: replicate on dedicated-03 vs prod-gpu-01 to confirm fleet-wide.
- TODO: instrument per-request kernel-path flag in traces (add small trace tag in runtime to mark when fallback occurs).

Notes to self
- When writing the Linear ticket, attach a short gif of the p99 time series (from telemetry) + the log window where kv_eviction_path appears.
- Ping driver team (Ravi) with host memory trace; include exact kernel versions.

References / quick links
- linear: TH-1423 (profiling artifacts uploaded)
- PR: serving-runtime#678 (work-in-progress: async kv reconciler prototype)
- slack: #runtime-debug thread: "thermocline event 10/2025" (search)

Last quick thought: the thermocline metaphor helps explain why clients see a sudden step rather than a smooth drift — once the working set crosses the boundary, shipping all requests through that slow path amplifies tail noise. Need to model how many concurrent heavy contexts the worker can safely hold before the boundary.

End of scratch-file.

-- Deb
